subject: Capacity & pilot path — Finovity recap
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Sam Cho <sam.cho@finovity.com>
Cc: Elaine Rhee <elaine@finovity.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: capacity + pilot path — Finovity / Redwood

Hi Sam / Elaine,

Thanks again for the call today — appreciated the candid breakdown of where Finovity is feeling the pain. Quick written recap so we have aligned next steps.

Who was on the call:
- Sam Cho (Finovity, ML Product)
- Elaine Rhee (Finovity, Platform)
- Priyom Das (Redwood, AE)

Key pain points you confirmed:
- Tail latency spikes for interactive assistants (esp. 512–1024 token flows) causing user-visible lag during market hours.
- High per-embedding costs for batch vectorization jobs (monthly spend unpredictable).
- Concerns about capacity predictability during quarter-end campaigns (traffic bursts).
- Need for clear data handling assurances for analytics pipelines (data-in-rest + retention policy).

Goals you articulated:
- Reduce per-embedding unit cost by ~35–45% through batching/quantization and dedicated routing.
- Bring 95th percentile latency under 150ms for 512-token workloads.
- Run a 4–6 week pilot (dedicated pool) to validate perf/cost before committing to reserved capacity.

New workloads mentioned:
- Nightly bulk embeddings for recommendation updates (~3M vectors / month).
- Real-time assistant queries during market hours (bursty, low-latency).

What Redwood will deliver next (by Jan 20):
1) A usage-backed cost proposal (see attached finovity-usage-q4.csv + RDW cost proposal v2).
2) Pilot plan: 4–6 week dedicated pool with automated prefix/KV caching and telemetry access.
3) Onboarding checklist for CS to validate success criteria (latency targets, token-cost targets, instrumentation).
4) Answers on SLA/data residency & contract items (I flagged procurement items to our legal team).

Immediate asks for you:
- Can procurement confirm the email for the formal quote/PO (cc'd procurement@finovity.com?)
- Exec sponsor availability for a short demo the week of Jan 26 (Sam mentioned possible availability).

Attachments: finovity-usage-q4.csv (usage extract), rdw-cost-proposal-v2.pdf (proposal stub).

If I missed anything or mis-ordered priorities, say so and I will update. I can schedule the pilot kickoff once procurement confirms quote path.

Thanks — Priyom

--
Priyom Das
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
pri.yom@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Thanks Priyom — this captures the discussion well. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Procurement contact is procurement@finovity.com (copied). They need the formal quote and headcount/seat-free details by COB Jan 22 to make timelines for Q1 budget.
- Executive sponsor (Maya Lin, VP Product) asked for a 30-minute demo and high-level cost summary on Wed Jan 27 or Thu Jan 28. Either day works but preference is Jan 27 afternoon.
- On SLA/data handling: can you confirm whether pilot traffic will be logged/retained by Redwood and for how long? We need a statement for our security team before kickoff.

Also confirming the pilot success criteria you wrote down: 95th latency <150ms and embedding cost reduction of ~40% — those are correct.

If you can turn around the cost proposal and a short one-pager on pilot telemetry (what metrics we'll see), procurement will expedite a PO.

Sam

Hi Sam / Elaine / procurement team,

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached is the updated RDW cost proposal (rdw-cost-proposal-v2.pdf) and a usage extract we generated from your Q4 pipeline (finovity-usage-q4.csv).

Concrete next steps we agreed: 
1) Redwood to provide a 4-week pilot (start window: week of Feb 2) — dedicated pool sized to current peak + 20% buffer.
2) Procurement to confirm PO path by Jan 22 so we can commit capacity.
3) Technical kickoff (30 min) w/ Finovity infra + Redwood infra — proposed Wed Jan 27 3:00 PM ET (calendar invite sent).
4) Success criteria: 95th perc latency < 150ms; embedding unit cost reduction >= 35%. Dashboard metrics will be shared within 48 hours of pilot start.

Answering the SLA/data handling question: pilot telemetry will include request-level latency and per-route token consumption. Logs containing PII will not be retained; default retention for pilot logs is 30 days unless you request a different policy. We'll include a short appendix in the legal/contract packet for procurement.

If the procurement team confirms PO routing (reply-all with next steps or DocuSign link), we will allocate the dedicated pool and schedule the kickoff.

Meeting link: https://calendar.redwood.com/meet/pri_yom-30
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/finovity/1423
